fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Current syntax is split between reusable argparse parsers, imperative argv loops, 54 hand-maintained package-help files, and 22 curated intercept descriptions. A registry alone would remove command-census drift but still allow the parser, runtime help, and documentation to disagree. This story establishes the one-parser contract and safe canonical help before execution routing moves off the compatibility ladder.

## Approach
Deliver this as four dependency-ordered child tasks:

1. Add the lean parser/route foundation: frozen route records, a side-effect-free argparse factory protocol, deterministic formatter policy, Rebar-compatible parse-error seam, registry validation, and derived compatibility exports. No route/help cutover yet.
2. Migrate core ticket/store/config/maintenance command families from imperative parsing or inline argparse construction to pure factories, switching each runtime handler in the same change and pinning accepted/rejected argv parity.
3. Migrate advanced bridge/reconciler/LLM/workflow/audit/identity command families similarly. Core and advanced migrations may proceed in parallel after the foundation.
4. After the complete route/parser census passes, generate committed package-help and grouped-overview bytes from those factories and cut top-level help/unknown routing to registry/package data before RP-04 operation/config/store/handler boundaries.

Factories are stdlib-only, accept deterministic `prog` input, and return argparse parsers used by runtime handlers and build/check generation. A shared ArgumentParser subclass/formatter may preserve Rebar's diagnostics and non-terminating library call shape; it must not become a new grammar engine. Manually describing syntax in docs, reconstructing grammar from source, or leaving runtime on an imperative parser after adding a factory is prohibited.

Registry validation rejects duplicate spellings, contradictory policy, unknown capabilities, alias/retired collisions, missing/stray generated resources, and absent parser references without importing command handlers. Full handler/factory reference resolution remains a build/full-extra check rather than normal startup.

Top-level routing recognizes only global config-prefix tokens, command identity, first-token help forms, and unknown commands. Nested parsing stays with the selected handler's factory. Generated artifacts use fixed width, formatter, `prog`, newline, and ordering so `--check` is byte-deterministic.

Exact aliases reuse canonical artifacts. Compatibility shims compose canonical argument-definition helpers with alias-specific `prog` and replacement epilog; `jira-onboard` keeps historical spelling. Hidden `bridge-status` resolves explicit help but stays undiscoverable; `purge-bridge` stays unknown.

## Compatibility and Rollback
The only approved public delta is safe canonical help/overview normalization. Each parser migration first captures production-path positive, negative, boundary, `--`, stream, exit-code, and diagnostic oracles, then switches runtime and factory atomically. Any other behavior delta requires an explicit ticket decision.

Expansion keeps derived compatibility exports and the old execution ladder. Generated help becomes authoritative only after all parser-family children close. Rollback reverts a parser family and its artifacts together; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Each child records its test tier and observable oracle. Pure registry/factory validation uses unit tests. Parser migrations use existing command interface tests strengthened with accepted/rejected argv matrices and nearest controls. Help cutover uses real CLI subprocesses in a fresh attachable checkout with sentinels that fail on operation snapshot, config, mount, handler resolution, or optional imports. Generator checks compare regenerated files byte-for-byte.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tasks are closed, and every registered command grammar is produced by one runtime-used side-effect-free argparse factory.
- [ ] No docs-only grammar, imperative runtime parser duplicated by a help factory, source-regex command grammar, or second parser framework remains.
- [ ] Every canonical visible command has byte-current generated package help and appears once in the generated grouped overview.
- [ ] Both top-level help forms and approved alias classes return generated bytes before operation/config/store/handler/optional-import boundaries; retired syntax remains unknown.
- [ ] Parser parity tests show no unapproved delta in accepted/rejected argv, `--`, diagnostics, streams, or exit codes.
- [ ] Existing command execution still uses the compatibility route ladder, while every selected handler now consumes its shared factory.
